paragraphs.text: An analysis file is created when a sample is added to a Set for the first time. This file contains analyzed audio data that allows Live to optimize the stretching quality when warping samples, as well as automatically detect the tempo of long samples. The analyzed data is also used to quickly draw the audio’s waveform in the Sample Editor.
For long samples, it may take a few moments for the analysis to complete. During the process, the audio waveform is grayed out until it is fully drawn, and the sample cannot be played back.
The analysis file is added to the same folder location as the original sample. It has the sample’s name along with the .asd extension.

Analysis files do not appear in Live’s browser, but you can tell if a sample has a corresponding .asd based on its browser icon. The icons for samples with an .asd have a small checkmark in the bottom right corner, while the icons for samples without an .asd do not.
You can use an analysis file to store default clip settings for a sample. To do so, click the Save Default Clip button in the clip’s title bar in Clip View.
Once saved, the sample loads with its default clip settings whenever it is added to a Set. This can be useful for retaining the same Warp Markers for a sample across different projects.

Clicking the Save Default Clip button for one clip does not affect any other clips that use the same sample in existing Sets. It is only when you import the sample again after saving that the analysis file is used to restore the clip settings. Note that saving a clip’s settings is different from saving an audio clip as a Live Clip, which also stores the clip’s devices.

The analysis process is enabled by default. A sample is not analyzed again if it already has an .asd file, and long samples are not analyzed if the Auto-Warp Long Samples option in the Record, Warp & Launch Settings is set to Off.

If you do not want an .asd file to be created when you load a sample, you can set the Create Analysis Files option in the File & Folder Settings to Off. In this case, samples will be analyzed each time they are loaded into a Set. Switching this option off does not delete any existing .asd files. Additionally, clicking the Save Default Clip button still generates an .asd file so that the clip settings can be stored.
